profile.headline:
Business systems
AI workflows
profile.intro: I turn business workflows into working software: inventory, barcode operations, knowledge-based support and content workbenches. I handle requirements, development and testing on independent projects, and contribute within my role on team projects.
profile.about: My project experience spans nonprofits, professional service firms and international brands, with work in requirements analysis, product planning, documentation and development.
profile.personality: I prefer to let my work speak for itself.
profile.background: On projects I lead, I use AI-assisted development and take responsibility for workflow design, testing and maintenance. On team projects, I contribute within the agreed division of work.

P01.title: Enterprise client projects
P01.summary: Contributed to nonprofit and law firm websites, an office system, UK brand marketing and AI support, with work on requirements, planning and demo development.
story: Turned client requirements into page designs and business workflows, working with the team on implementation.
Developed software on team client projects; other members conducted onsite discovery. For the RAG support project, I also organized the knowledge base, configured retrieval and tested the system.

P02.title: Shenzhen charity foundation
P02.summary: Contributed to a nonprofit website, organizing the foundation profile, charitable programs, news and public disclosures into a clear navigation structure.
story: The website needed to bring the foundation’s information into one place for visitors.
Developed the nonprofit website based on requirements gathered by the team.
Built foundation, program, news and public-disclosure sections, connecting the homepage with content pages.
The two first-phase websites were delivered and accepted in about one month. Positive client feedback led to a second phase of work on an internal system.
P02.process: The two first-phase websites were delivered and accepted in about one month. Positive client feedback led to a second-phase office system.

P03.title: Shenzhen law firm website
P03.summary: Contributed to a law firm website, bringing together services, lawyer profiles, news and inquiry channels through a coherent content structure.
story: Visitors needed to understand services and the lawyer team, and find an inquiry route.
Developed the law firm website based on requirements gathered by the team.
Built service, lawyer and news pages, with a consistent section structure and inquiry routes.
The two first-phase websites were delivered and accepted in about one month. Positive client feedback led to a second phase of work on an internal system.
P03.process: I developed the law firm website as part of the first phase, organizing services, lawyer profiles and recognition into clear content and navigation. The two websites were delivered and accepted in about one month. Positive feedback led to further work on the internal office system.

P04.title: Law firm office system
P04.summary: Developed an office system from the team’s onsite discovery, adapting workflows and scattered records to staff needs and contributing to training and handover.
story: The firm needed to organize office workflows and scattered records around staff roles.
I developed the office system from the team’s onsite interviews and discovery.
Business requirements, product documentation and office system demo interfaces.

The second phase took more than three months, covering development, user training and handover. The client reported less time spent on routine work and lower software costs; no quantified data was provided.
P04.process: Developed from team discovery, the second phase took over three months through training and handover. The client reported less time spent and lower software costs, without quantitative data.

P05.title: UK water purification brand marketing
P05.summary: Contributed to international brand marketing through campaigns, content and AI video production, creator partnerships and social promotion around the client’s own website.
story: Presented water purification products, use cases and brand information consistently for an international audience.
The team shared planning, content, AI video and promotion work; the client owned the website.
Produced campaign and brand content, AI videos and KOC collaborations, with Facebook, Instagram and TikTok promotion directing visitors to the client’s site.
The project ran for more than three months. Once operations stabilized, the client took over; no conversion or sales growth data was provided.
P05.process: The team worked for over three months, using KOC collaborations and social channels to direct visitors to the client’s website. The client took over after stable operation; conversion and sales data were not provided.

P06.title: AI order entry interaction prototype
P06.summary: Built an order entry prototype demonstrating uploads, field display, manual corrections, status filters and audit logs, supported by workflow and requirements documentation.
story: Used an interactive prototype to validate document uploads, field entry, manual corrections and result review.
Interactive demonstrations of uploading, field display, manual corrections, status filters and audit logs.

P07.title: Furniture brand website
P07.summary: Led development of a website for international buyers, combining product, factory and gallery content with language switching and a structured inquiry flow.
story: Helped international buyers understand the products, factory and brand through the website.
Led requirements analysis and workflow design, used AI-assisted development, and handled testing and ongoing maintenance.
An English brand website with product and factory information, a gallery and language switching.
Organized product, factory, brand and gallery material into an English front end with language switching. Models, dimensions and specifications are covered in a separate product catalog.
Used desktop and mobile previews to review the information structure and reading paths. Brand presentation, content administration and inquiry permissions are separate scopes.
The available work includes the brand front end, website files, a delivery package and desktop/mobile previews. CMS content editing and inquiry permissions are separated in the requirements.
This page shows an anonymized desktop preview; the related case covers the product catalog. Front-end presentation and back-end functions are described separately.

P08.title: Furniture product catalog
P08.summary: Organized product images, models, dimensions and specifications into print and mobile catalogs, distinguishing real product photos from generated scene imagery.
story: Presented product images, models, dimensions and specifications together so buyers could compare products.
Led requirements analysis and workflow design, used AI-assisted development, and handled testing and ongoing maintenance.
Separate print and mobile reading layouts for product images, models, dimensions and specifications.

P09.title: Furniture barcode inventory system
P09.summary: Led a carton-based barcode inventory system, designing receiving, transfers and dispatch with permissions, duplicate-submission handling and correction flows.
story: Carton-based stock across locations needed connected receiving, transfer, dispatch and correction flows, without duplicate entries on retries.
I led requirements and workflow design, used AI-assisted development, and handled testing and maintenance.
Implemented carton scanning, receiving, transfers, dispatch and reversals, with identity checks, duplicate-request handling and insufficient-stock checks.

Checked the full inventory sequence, then duplicate requests, insufficient stock and cancelled-request retries. Transfers cross-check both locations and total stock; corrections link to the original document.
Delivered to the client, covering barcode receiving, transfers, dispatch and corrections. The technical section describes the implementation.
P09.process: Checked the inventory sequence, duplicate requests, shortages and cancelled retries, then delivered the system to the client.

P10.title: Sanitaryware manufacturer inventory system
P10.summary: Independently developed and delivered an inventory system for a large B2B sanitaryware manufacturer, covering requirements, workflow analysis and implementation.
story: The client needed inventory management connected to product variants, purchasing, returns and stocktakes. Quantities and statuses must agree with the actual business operations.
Independently handled requirements, workflow analysis, development on the existing foundation and delivery.
Adapted an existing foundation for inventory, connecting PC and H5 entry points with reference data, purchasing, stock and business overview pages.
Defined the scope after a half-day requirements discussion. With limited later client communication, I continued from the initial discovery and industry understanding.
Cross-checked documents, stock and transactions rather than relying on a success message. A stocktake example appears below.
Delivered the system in about two months. Quantified usage outcomes are not available.
P10.process: Adapted the foundation after a half-day requirements discussion. Reviews cross-check documents, stock and transactions. Delivered in about two months.

P11.title: UK and Australia small business website experiments
P11.summary: Researched public information on small businesses, built website redesign demos, checked mobile browsing and inquiry flows, and prepared quotes and collaboration materials.
story: Small business websites need coherent content, mobile experiences and inquiry flows.

P12.title: Zhijing · AI content workbench
P12.summary: Led a content workbench for furnishing fabrics, organizing product facts, style settings, editing and human review while validating model output, account connection and export separately.
story: Fabric businesses need content based on product images, specifications and account style. Human review remains part of the flow to keep content aligned with product facts.
I led requirements and workflow design, used AI-assisted development, and handled testing and maintenance.
The workbench covers setup, style confirmation, product input, editing, human review and export. The image shows product input.
Product facts, content capabilities, human approval and output paths are organized and validated separately. A successful account connection is not treated as evidence of a complete generation flow.

August 2026 records cover a text probe and account login, restart, disconnection and login again. The full-content test failed at delivery of its first image; end-to-end generation and RED publishing have not passed.
P12.process: Validated content and account connection separately. Login, restart and disconnection records exist; the full-content test failed at its first image, and generation and publishing have not passed end to end.

P13.title: Pocket Rove
P13.summary: Led a bilingual daily task app with completion tracking, history and souvenirs, adding notification and payment entry points and preparing App Store presentation assets.

Led requirements analysis and workflow design, used AI-assisted development, and handled testing and ongoing maintenance.

P14.summary: Developed a pet companion focus app with pet adoption, duration goals and state transitions, integrating permissions, Live Activities and notifications.
story: Explored a gentler focus experience by incorporating a pet companion into the workflow.

P15.title: PetSocial (now HelloTail)
P15.summary: Developed pet profiles, photo displays, discovery invitations and chat, handling message sending and recovery after restart with a separate experience demo.
story: Pet profiles provide a starting point for discovery, invitations, owner connections and text conversations.
I developed the entire project.
The native iOS app connects pet profiles, photos, invitations, owner connections and chat, including message state and restart recovery. The separate VisualDemo presents UI and interactions only.

An October 5, 2026 regression on my iPhone covered profiles, connections and chat history. A technical test message appeared once; after termination and restart, the session and message were restored from the service.

The native candidate is iterating as HelloTail, with local builds, installation on my device and partial verification. Cross-device receipt, notification delivery, physical-device performance and release completion remain unverified; installation or demo images do not establish an App Store release.
P15.process: I developed this native iOS pet-social project, now iterating under the name HelloTail, connecting pet profiles, discovery invitations and chat. A separate VisualDemo presents the experience. The cover comes from that demo; native implementation and device validation are described separately.
P15.imageNote: Independent VisualDemo discovery screen · demo profiles, not real community users

The support interface provides a welcome message, quick options, question input and contact routes.

Available material includes the owner’s project account and the initial support interface, showing the welcome message, quick support, question input and contact entry. Answer quality and retrieval performance require corresponding answer and retrieval records.
